For EBRPD Board Director · Ward 3
# William Yragui for East Bay Regional Park District Ward 3
Protecting the places that bring us together.
William Yragui is running for East Bay Regional Park District Board Director in Ward 3 to keep our parks welcoming, resilient, and accountable.
Join the campaignExplore the vision
Discover more ↓
Meet William
## Stewardship rooted in community.
Our parks are more than destinations. They are where families gather, young people discover nature, and neighbors find common ground.
William is running for the East Bay Regional Park District Board to bring a practical, community-first voice to Ward 3. His campaign is centered on careful stewardship, safe and equitable access, climate resilience, and transparent decisions.
The work ahead
## Parks that thrive
for generations.
01
### Protect open space
Safeguard habitat, watersheds, and the natural landscapes that define the East Bay.
02
### Welcome every community
Improve safe, equitable access and create park experiences that work for people of all ages and abilities.
03
### Prepare for a changing climate
Invest in wildfire readiness, resilient landscapes, and responsible long-term maintenance.
04
### Lead with accountability
Make decisions transparently, listen consistently, and protect public resources with care.
Know your district
## Ward 3 is our shared landscape.
Ward 3 includes Castro Valley, Hayward, Union City, and part of Fremont. Explore the official East Bay Regional Park District map to learn whether your community is in the district.
Open the official map ↗
Niles CanyonPleasanton RidgeVargas PlateauView from Vargas Plateau towards Mission PeakCull Canyon Regional ParkGarin Regional Park Apple Festival
“These places belong to all of us—and their future depends on what we do together.”
William Yragui
Community support
## Endorsements.
Neighbors across Ward 3 are standing with William.
Endorsement summary
### Broad support across the East Bay
William is endorsed by respected environmental and Democratic organizations, current and former regional park leaders, recreation-district directors, elected officials, conservation advocates, educators, business owners, and community volunteers.

### Susie Claxton
Fremont · Park Advisory Committee, Advisor, Ward 3
“William has a long and strong history of working to preserve and enhance the natural settings we are so privileged to live near. As a physician, I know the importance that exercise and being close to nature has on our physical and mental well-being. Of all the candidates running for EBRPD Ward 3, I trust William the most for the health of our community, parks, and ecosystem.”
### Tri Do
Hayward · Public Health Physician
“William Yragui is one of the best prepared candidates for any office I have met - ever! His knowledge of how East Bay Regional Parks functions, its limitations, its goals and possible funding sources to meet unfulfilled dreams is truly impressive. He will serve as a great asset for park users in the TriCity area as he is passionate about improving the park experience for all and having more residents get into our regional parks. I hope to work with him and the Board on continuing challenges for wildfire mitigation.”
### Bob Wieckowski
Fremont · None
“Mr. Yragui's decisions and values about our local parks, especially increasing accessibility for all residents to our local parks is paramount and match my own.”
### Steven Coulthard
Glenmoor Gardens / Fremont · Local Businessman / Past Exalted Ruler - Fremont Elks Lodge
“William’s goals match my expectations for future management of present and future EB regional parks and open spaces. William has protected Open Space; a precious sanctuary for wildlife habitat while providing a place for us to be restored through nature.”
### Mary Clements
Hayward · Member of Save Skywest Open Space Task Force
### Leslie Goldstein
Berkeley/El Cerrito · Contracts and Grants Director, UC Berkeley- El Cerrito Parks and Recreation Commissioner (2009-2014), Friends of Wildcat Canyon Park
### Joyce Norton-Jones
Castro Valley · Nurse Practitioner, Women's Health

Richmond · Sierra Club West Contra Costa Group Chair, Sprawldef
“I am proud to endorse William for EBRPD Board Ward 3.”
### Mark Van Landuyt
Danville · The Young Turks & 4Dore Productions, Inc
“Wlliam’s devotion to East Bay public lands is relentless, as demonstrated by the time and effort he spent onboarding me as a Sierra Club hiking leader. I enthusiastically endorse William for EBRPD Ward 3.”
### Erik Sommargren
Livermore · Water policy analyst and geologist
“William, as Chair of the South Alameda County Group, and I, as Chair of the Tri-Valley Group, of the Sierra Club, have worked together on environmental issues. William has led hundreds of outings in EBRPD parks and his knowledge of those parks is comprehensive. Likewise, he has led hikes in the Mission Peak Conservancy with his co-founders since 2014. I highly recommend William as a Director of Ward 3 on the EBRPD Board.”
### Carol Silva
Livermore · Sierra Club Tri Valley Group Chair
“I think William would be a great addition to the EBRPD Board.”
### Shirley Lewandowski
Dublin · Sierra Club Tri Valley Group ExCom
“You are the right choice, based on years of experience working to improve our parks and access to open space.”
### Gary Wolff
Castro Valley · Water Resources Engineer & Economist EBMUD Candidate
“William has demonstrated a genuine commitment to our parks, open spaces, and the communities that enjoy them. I appreciate his hands-on involvement, practical approach, and willingness to listen to residents. His years of advocacy and community service bring valuable experience to the East Bay Regional Park District.”
### Vipin Sharma
Fremont · Candidate for Fremont City Council District 3 2026
“William has a true passion to protect the parks we love dearly. I am proud to endorse William.”
### Sarabjit Cheema
Union City · Teacher, Former Trustee for New Haven Schools
“Experience!!!”
### Murphy McCalley
Castro Valley · AC Transit Board Director
### Aziz Akbari
Fremont · Board President, Alameda County Water District
### Donald Wong
Fremont
“William is a great neighbor and has done a lot for our community. He regularly organizes and volunteers for hikes, taking the time to share his knowledge about Mission Peak and other trails around Fremont. He genuinely enjoys bringing people together and giving back to the community. I’m happy to endorse him!”
### SATHISH SRINIVASAN
Fremont
“I know William to be honest, conscientious, and to believe in wildlife conservation. That's exactly what we need on the EBRPD board!”
### Mike Vandeman
Berkeley · Machine-Free Trails Association
### Raj Salwan
Fremont · City of Fremont, Mayor
“He will represent me and my interests.”
### Moina Shaiq
fremont
“William Yragui has years of community organizing experience and is broadly connected to groups and individuals working on conservation and related causes. He'll be ready to hit the ground running on the EBRPD board.”
### Lisa Danz
San Francisco, formerly Fremont
“When wealthy property owners blackmailed the East Bay Regional Parks District into improving the roads leading to their properties near the Vargas Plateau by suing in court and in doing so denied Fremont residents access to the park for years, William was there to fight them. When NIMBY home owners near Mission Peak Park lobbied the City of Fremont into issuing parking tickets to Fremont residents who parked in their neighborhood when the tiny park parking lot overflowed, after a couple of those same NIMBYs sued the park to block an increase in the size of the parking lot because they claimed it ruined their view, William was there to fight them. William is getting my vote. If you care about maintaining local park access in the face of monied interests' ongoing attempts the deny access, he should get your vote too.”
### Jeffrey Haran
Fremont
“I have known William for over 15 years and cofounded Mission Peak Conservancy with him. He is an effective advocate for maintaining and improving access to public lands. He is pragmatic and seeks solutions that properly balance the public use and preservation needs for public lands. William is also an effective public speaker and writer and can communicate policy and need to a wide audience. He has written numerous op-eds in print media that concisely outlines the issues and effective policy suggestions to address public concerns. William will be an excellent public advocate and I hope he has the opportunity to serve.”
### Lawrence Edelson
Fremont · Mission Peak Conservancy
“For the last 15 years William has advocated for access and protection for our open spaces. No one has been a stronger and consistent advocate or has spent as much effort working with government agencies and others to enhance public access for all users of our East Bay parks. He spends multiple days per week in our East Bay Regional Parks and has advocated for expanding trails like Bay Ridge and the proposed Niles Canyon Trail to increase hiking and biking opportunities in the Southern East Bay.”
### Steve Skala
Fremont · Fmr. Member Fremont Bicycle and Pedestrian Technical Advisory Committee
“Over the past ten years of working closely with William, I’ve seen firsthand his unwavering integrity, passion, and commitment to the county's open spaces. His dedication and work ethic are unmatched—he is constantly going above and beyond, often following up late into the evening and on weekends. I recommend him without hesitation.”
### Lisa Barboza
San Jose · Sierra Club Loma Prieta = Guadlupe Regional Group Chair, also, Chapter Chair, Outings
“William is very passionate about expanding public access to open spaces and parks and has been advocating for easier trail access to parks and open spaces for many years. If you see him on the trails, you will see him picking up trash and dog poop almost on a daily basis. He truly is the best person to represent us.”
### Monica Melville
Fremont, CA · Past Co-President of Mission High School PTA (MPPFA)
“I have known William for the last few years and his support to the community is unwavering. I have joined his monthly hikes and seen how he uses the opportunity to being others into the folds of nature. He also voices the concern of the community in various forum and educates us on pros of any action being taken and its impact.”
### Tushar Agarwal
Fremont
“I appreciate William’s understanding of how agriculture and parks share our working landscape and must function together. William “gets it,” he understands the synergy among agriculture, trails, and wildlife management that defines our working landscapes.”
### Larry Gosselin
Livermore · Doctor Of Veterinary Medicine/CEO Sustainable Food Network LLC
“As a neighbor who has joined William on hikes, I have personally witnessed his deep dedication to, advocacy for, and care of the East Bay’s parks and natural spaces.”
### Nathan Fo
Fremont
“With William Yragui we have an opportunity to bring a true environmental champion with deep experience to the East Bay Regional Park District Board.”
### Eric Brooks
San Francisco · SF Bay Shoreline Contamination Cleanup Coalition - Co-Coordinator
“William puts his boots on the trail, his eyes on the ecosystems, and his whole heart in the park district.”
### Richard Bangert
Alameda · Alameda Point Environmental Report
“Congratulations! You must be one of the best candidates for any park district anywhere.”
### Jim Keller
San Jose · Hiker, Snowboarder, Kite flyer
“I know William personally. He is one of the most socially responsible person.”

“Best of luck - truly.”
